# Proposal 5 · §21–25 State model → recommendation

DESIGN PROPOSAL · PART 5 OF 5 · §21–25

## 21 Product state model

```
App
├── Library
└── Reader(book)
    ├── Chrome ............. Immersive ⇄ Controls visible
    ├── Docked panel (0–1) . None | Navigator: Contents · Search · Notes · extension tab
    ├── Floating layer (0–1) None | Aa | Go to | Selection bar → Note card | Peek | Image | ⌘K
    └── Orthogonal ......... Pages | Scroll · Theme · Full screen
```

- **One floating layer.** Opening one closes the current one. The docked Navigator is layout, not a layer, so it can sit beside one floating layer. Below 1100 px the Navigator floats and joins that single slot.
- **Chrome and Navigator alternate.** Opening the Navigator hides the bars; its header carries Library, the book title and progress.
- **Focus comes home.** Closing any layer returns focus to the text at the same reading position.
- **Messages queue.** One bottom-centre message at a time, newest first; timers pause on hover or focus.
- **Esc pops exactly one level:** floating layer → Navigator → chrome. It never leaves the book.
- **A page turn** closes floating layers (a note card saves first) and hides the chrome; the Navigator stays.
- **Selection wins:** starting a selection dismisses popovers and peeks.
- **Only modals suspend reading input** (⌘K, dialogs).
- **Search marks exist only while Search is open.**
- **Per-book memory:** position, layout mode and whether the Navigator was docked S2.

## 22 Edge cases and failure modes

| Failure | User impact | Prevention | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Extremely long chapter | Slow open, janky turns | Paginate near the viewport first; virtual sections | Approximate locations (“≈”) settle silently |
| Missing metadata | “Unknown” books, blank covers | Title from first heading or file name; generated cover | Edit title and author in Book info |
| Broken or missing TOC | No way to navigate | nav → NCX → heading scan → spine list | Contents is labelled “Generated from headings” |
| Invalid publisher CSS | Tiny, low-contrast or fixed-width text | Sanitiser, comfort overrides, contrast check on computed colours | Publisher styles setting (1.1); per-book “Simplify styles” |
| Corrupted book | Can’t open | Validate on import; tolerate damaged entries | Error card: Read anyway (damaged chapters marked) or Show file |
| Unsupported font | Missing glyphs | 1.5 s load timeout; glyph coverage check | Fall back to Literata; no prompt |
| Layout breaks after a font change | Lost place, overflow | Anchor-based reflow; images and tables constrained | Position kept; Back chip if the anchor moved |
| Slow search indexing | Incomplete results | Current chapter first; streamed results | Progress in the header; results fill in |
| Annotation anchors break | Highlights vanish or drift | CFI + text quote with prefix / suffix; fuzzy re-anchoring | “Couldn’t place” group with manual re-attach |
| Plugin crash or hang | Missing actions, freezes | Isolation, timeouts, budgets | Inline “stopped” line; auto-suspend; safe mode |
| Aggressive resizing | Flicker, CPU spikes | Debounce; reflow the current chapter only | Anchor kept |
| Rapid page turns | Skipped pages, lag | At most one queued turn; neighbours pre-rendered | Position always consistent |
| Trackpad momentum | Several pages flipped | One turn per gesture; momentum ignored | Back chip after fast multi-page moves |
| Save failure | Lost progress or notes | Write-ahead log, atomic writes | Banner “Couldn’t save notes · Retry”; nothing discarded |

## 23 Competitive design references

| Reference | Adopt | Avoid | Generalised principle |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Apple Books** | A small Aa popover; calm themes; full-screen reading | Page curl; store promotion near the reading flow | A few good options beat a settings page |
| **Kindle** | Tap zones; Go to location; look-ups that keep your place | Recommendations inside the reader; closed formats | Look things up without leaving the page |
| **Kobo** | Deeper typography behind an “advanced” step; opt-in stats | Dense settings on first reveal | Depth one step away, never on top |
| **Readwise Reader** | Keyboard-first annotation, H to highlight, ⌘K, strong export | Many features competing with the text | Accelerators and a palette keep chrome small |
| **Calibre** | Format robustness; a broad plugin ecosystem | Library-centric dense UI; plugins with full system access | Managing and reading are different jobs |
| **Thorium** | EPUB 3 accessibility, fixed layout, standards support | Heavy dialogs and chrome | Standards compliance is a UX feature |
| **Foliate** | Native look; good desktop pagination; dictionary look-up | Assumptions tied to one platform | Feel native on each platform |
| **Browsers** | Find bar with counts and ⌘G; Back history; reader-mode measure; per-host permissions | Toolbar and tab clutter | Every jump is reversible |
| **Code editors** | Manifest contribution points, lazy activation, isolated extension host, command palette, safe mode | Unbounded toolbar and status-bar contributions | Declarative slots, lazy and isolated |

## 24 Recommended screen set

| Screen | Purpose · main components | Visually dominant | Kept quiet |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 Library | Choose or resume: Continue reading, cover grid, search, sort | Current book, Resume | Sort, Open…, item menus |
| 02 Reader — immersive | Read: page, text, one location line | Text | Everything else is absent |
| 03 Reader — controls | Orient and reach tools: top bar, scrubber, margin chevrons | Text, then title and progress | Icons in secondary ink |
| 04 Contents | Navigate: book header, tabs, chapter list | Current chapter | Other entries |
| 05 Search | Find: field, count, grouped snippets, marks in text | Active result, in list and page | Collapsed chapters, hints |
| 06 Selection | Act on text: the selection bar | The selected text | The bar sits above, never over it |
| 07 Margin note | Write: margin card, autosave | The note | Colour, delete, save state |
| 08 Notes | Revisit: filters, grouped quotes, “Couldn’t place” | Quotes | Dates, counts, export |
| 09 Reading settings | Adjust comfort: size, theme, spacing, layout | Size control | Link to Preferences |
| 10 Themes | Paper, Sepia and Night, highlights included | Text contrast | Token labels |
| 11 Extensions | Manage: list, toggles, permissions, status | Permissions and status | Versions, descriptions |
| 12 Empty and error states | Recover: empty library, damaged book, extension failure, toasts | The recovery action | Explanations |
| 13 Tablet | Touch model: tap zones and gestures | Text | Zone overlay (spec only) |
| 14 Night controls | Chrome and selection bar on dark ground | Text; inverted selection bar | Icons, hairlines |
| 15 Narrow window | Compact bar; note as bottom sheet | The note and its passage | Icon-only chrome |
| 16 Command palette | Long-tail commands, Recently closed, extension commands with shortcuts | Query and active row | Sources, shortcut hints |
| 17 Footnote · Go to | Peek anchored to the marker; Go to by %, chapter or page | Note text; the target | Secondary actions |

## 25 Final recommendation

| **1 · Product philosophy** | A reader, not a manager. Text first, tools summoned where you’re reading, extensions as guests. |
|---|---|
| **2 · Information architecture** | Two pages (Library, Reader); one Navigator sidebar with three tabs; popovers for settings; contextual bars on text; ⌘K for the long tail; Preferences in its own window. |
| **3 · Reader layout** | One centred column clamped to 56–74 characters; margins absorb extra width; pages snap to whole lines; two-page spread from 1480 px; Paper, Sepia, Night. |
| **4 · Navigation** | Edge reveal and centre tap; keys and tap zones for pages; **[ ]** for chapters; history with a Back chip after every jump; footnotes as peeks. |
| **5 · Reading mode** | Pages by default; Scroll as the single alternative, remembered per book; one turn per gesture. |
| **6 · Annotation** | Select → one-click colour saves → margin note that autosaves → Notes tab. Undo instead of confirmations; two anchors per highlight. |
| **7 · MVP** | The twelve required features plus one exporter (Markdown). No sync, accounts, AI, TTS, store or social. |
| **8 · Plugin architecture** | Manifest contribution points, lazy activation, isolated workers and sandboxed frames, capability permissions, a watchdog and safe mode. |
| **9 · Key constraints** | No reader transition over 250 ms; one floating layer; no permanent chrome; AAA contrast for body text and ≥ 3:1 for every meaningful mark; no meaning by colour alone; every single key has a modified twin; extensions never touch the page. |

### The ten most important design decisions

- The reader opens immersive, with no permanent chrome.
- Controls appear on an edge, a centre tap or Tab, and hide on the next page turn.
- Pages is the default mode; Scroll is the only alternative.
- One wheel notch or trackpad gesture turns at most one page; momentum is ignored.
- Contents, Search and Notes share one Navigator sidebar.
- Every jump can be undone through a history stack and a visible Back chip.
- A highlight takes one click; notes live in the margin; deletes use Undo, not dialogs.
- The Aa popover has four controls; anything more must earn its place.
- The publisher decides structure; the reader decides comfort.
- Extensions get slots and permissions, never the page — and a broken one can never stop you reading.
Library → Book → Reading Canvas → Contextual Tools → Extensions

Optimised in this order: reading immersion → clarity → interaction predictability → reading comfort → extensibility
